chapter: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
name: Universal Adult Franchise

scenes.animation: A busy street during election season: newspaper headlines flutter past, and people with inked fingers smile at the camera. Zippy, holding a newspaper upside down, looks confused while Neo points at a banner reading 'General Elections 2024'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: It's just voting! Why is the whole country so excited?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Just voting? It's the biggest celebration of our democracy, the general elections!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 2024, over 968 million voters were eligible to vote for the 543 constituencies of the Lok Sabha.

scenes.animation: A glossary card flips open: 'Franchise = a right granted by the constitution or government (also called suffrage)'. Below it, a long queue of very different citizens forms: a farmer, a doctor, a student, an elderly woman. Each holds up one identical ballot marked '1 vote = equal value'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Franchise means a right granted by the constitution or government. Another word for it is suffrage.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Universal adult franchise means every adult citizen gets one vote, and all votes have equal value.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Every Indian citizen aged 18 and above can vote, irrespective of caste, creed, race, religion, gender, education or income. That is what 'universal' means.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the richest person and a chaiwala both get exactly one vote?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly. And no one can vote on another person's behalf.

scenes.animation: A horizontal timeline builds from left to right: 'Before Independence: about 13% could vote', 'From the start: universal adult franchise in the Constitution', '1988: voting age lowered from 21 to 18'. A small tag reads 'Article 326'. A voter-registration card slides in with the word 'Registered in your constituency'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Before Independence, only around 13 per cent of Indians were allowed to vote.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Constitution makers made universal adult franchise a feature of Indian democracy right from the outset. It is in Article 326.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 1988, India lowered the minimum voting age from 21 to 18.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: To vote, you must be registered as a voter in your constituency, an area whose voters elect a representative.

scenes.animation: A world map lights up country by country. A 1913 women's suffrage parade marches across the USA; Switzerland glows with the label '1971'. India glows from the very start with the label 'Women voted from the beginning'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Did women have to fight for their vote here too?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In many countries, yes. Women in Switzerland got the vote only in 1971.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In India, a progressive constitutional vision and deep democratic values ensured women could vote from the very beginning.

scenes.animation: A mindmap builds from a central bubble 'Why universal adult franchise?'. Branches pop out one by one: 'Everyone is equal', 'Everyone's voice matters', 'Power to determine one's future', 'Fosters civic engagement', 'Representatives answerable to voters'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker lands on the 'Everyone is equal' branch.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 1947, our literacy rate was only about 14 per cent. Some argued that only literate people should vote.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: But the Constitution makers trusted the common citizen. Universal franchise means everyone is equal and everyone's voice matters.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It gives people the power to decide their future, and representatives become answerable to voters, who can vote them out.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: when asked why universal adult franchise matters, give at least two clear reasons, like equality and accountability.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a ballot-box icon. Points appear one by one: '1. Every citizen 18+ gets one vote of equal value', '2. Adopted from the start; age lowered from 21 to 18 in 1988', '3. Ensures equality, voice and accountability'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: universal adult franchise gives every citizen aged 18 and above one vote of equal value.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: India adopted it right from the start, and lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 in 1988.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: it ensures equality, gives everyone a voice, and keeps leaders answerable.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I'm counting the days till I turn 18!

chapter: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
name: Bridging Barriers: Ensuring Everyone Can Vote

scenes.animation: A jeep bumps up a snowy mountain road carrying polling officials and a voting machine. Zippy peeks out of a crate. At the top, a tiny polling booth is set up for one woman voter, who waves happily.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: All this trouble for just one voter? Seriously?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Seriously. In a democracy, no voter should be left behind.

scenes.animation: A comparison graphic: a crowd of Indian voters labelled '15x' stands next to a small crowd labelled 'UK population'; then an outline of India beside France labelled 'India = 6x larger in area'. Mountains, deserts and islands pop up on an India map to show geographic diversity.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: India is large, diverse and complex. Our eligible voters are fifteen times the population of the United Kingdom.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: India is also six times larger than France in area, with mountains, deserts and islands.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Election Commission of India organises elections, keeping all this in mind.

scenes.animation: Icons appear one by one around a polling booth: an elderly man voting from home, a postal envelope, a braille voter card, a phone app requesting a wheelchair, and a ramp. A banner reads 'Removing barriers'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The ECI takes special steps to remove barriers. Officials travel to remote places so every citizen can vote.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 2024, for the first time, the elderly and people with disabilities could vote from home.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: There were braille-enabled voter cards, postal voting for some voters, and app-based requests for wheelchairs and ramps.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: But did everyone actually vote?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: No. About 34 per cent of eligible voters did not vote in 2024. That is something to think about.

scenes.animation: A classroom at Suryodaya School. Three candidate cards appear: Ahmed (cleanliness poster), Gurmat (peer coaching noticeboard), Ravi (lunchtime music show). Ms. Usha wears an 'Election Officer' badge and sets up a voting corner with a ballot box and a braille ballot for Neha.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Let's see an election in a Grade 8 class. Ahmed, Gurmat and Ravi contest for Class Representative.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Their teacher, Ms. Usha, is the Election Officer. She explains the secret ballot, so no one knows who voted for whom.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She even arranges a braille ballot paper for Neha.

scenes.animation: The sealed box opens while Ms. Sheeba watches. A bar chart builds: Ahmed 8, Gurmat 12, Ravi 10, plus one grey slip marked 'Invalid'. Gurmat's bar glows gold. A side card slides in: 'NOTA = None Of The Above'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Thirty-three votes were cast. One unmarked paper was invalid. Ahmed got 8, Gurmat 12 and Ravi 10.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Gurmat, with the most votes, became Class Representative.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: What if I didn't like any candidate?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: India offers NOTA, None Of The Above. It doesn't change the result, but it tells everyone that voters want better choices.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: a secret ballot means your vote is private, so you can choose freely without fear. This is a favourite question.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a wheelchair ramp icon, a braille card and a sealed ballot box. Points appear: '1. ECI removes barriers: home voting, braille, postal votes', '2. Secret ballot keeps voting private and fair', '3. NOTA lets voters reject all candidates'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: the ECI removes barriers with home voting, braille cards, postal votes and help like ramps.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: a secret ballot keeps every vote private and the election fair.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: NOTA lets a voter reject all candidates without changing the result.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Congratulations, Gurmat! Now please fix our timetable.

chapter: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
name: The Election Commission of India

scenes.animation: Zippy stands in front of a mountain of numbers: '968 million voters', '543 constituencies', 'over 1 million polling stations'. The numbers topple onto him like a pile of books.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Who on earth manages an election this big?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Election Commission of India, or ECI. Let's meet it.

scenes.animation: The ECI building in Delhi appears with a nameplate. Cards flip in: 'Independent constitutional body', 'Established 1950', 'First general elections: 1951-52'. Then four task icons pop up: a calendar, a party registration form, a rulebook labelled 'MCC', and an eye overseeing everything.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The ECI is an independent constitutional body that conducts free and fair elections. It was established in 1950.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It conducts elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, state legislative assemblies, and the offices of the President and Vice President.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It sets election dates, registers political parties, enforces the Model Code of Conduct and oversees the whole process.

scenes.animation: A flowchart builds top-down in three levels: 'National: Chief Election Commissioner + two Election Commissioners' then 'State/UT: Chief Electoral Officer' then 'District: District Election Officer', which splits into 'Returning Officer (conducts elections)' and 'Electoral Registration Officer (manages voter list)'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: At the national level, there is a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Each state or union territory has a Chief Electoral Officer, and each district has a District Election Officer.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Below them, the Returning Officer conducts elections, and the Electoral Registration Officer manages the voter list.

scenes.animation: A polling booth in four steps, animated as Zippy moves through: officer 1 checks the voter list and ID; officer 2 inks his finger, gives a chit and takes a signature; officer 3 takes the chit and checks the ink; at the EVM, Zippy presses a button, hears a beep and sees a slip in the VVPAT window.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Here's how you vote. The first polling officer checks your name and ID.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The second inks your finger, gives a chit and takes your signature. The third takes the chit and checks your finger.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then you press a button on the electronic voting machine, or EVM, and hear a beep. The VVPAT shows a printed slip so you can verify your vote.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Beep! I voted! Well, pretend-voted.

scenes.animation: A rulebook titled 'Model Code of Conduct' opens with three rules: 'No new schemes by the government during elections', 'Restraint and peace', 'No gifts for votes'. A red cross stamps a scene of a candidate handing out sarees. A portrait card of T.N. Seshan slides in with 'CEC from 1990: voter IDs, spending checks'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Model Code of Conduct lists dos and don'ts for parties and candidates.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The government cannot announce new schemes to influence voters, candidates must keep the peace, and giving gifts for votes is punishable.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The code was first adopted in Kerala in 1960. T.N. Seshan, Chief Election Commissioner from 1990, brought reforms like voter IDs to stop proxy voting.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: remember the full form VVPAT, Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail. It gives a paper backup for checking votes.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the ECI logo-style icon of a ballot box. Points appear: '1. ECI: independent constitutional body, set up in 1950', '2. Voting: 3 polling officers, then EVM + VVPAT', '3. Model Code of Conduct keeps elections fair'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: the ECI is an independent constitutional body, set up in 1950, that runs free and fair elections.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: a voter passes three polling officers, then votes on the EVM and checks the VVPAT slip.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the Model Code of Conduct keeps parties and candidates in line during elections.

chapter: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
name: Elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies

scenes.animation: A festival scene with lights and rangoli, but instead of diyas, voters hold up inked fingers. A banner reads 'Festival of Democracy'. Zippy dances with a sparkler.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: A festival? Where are the sweets?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Elections are called the Festival of Democracy. The treat is choosing your own representatives freely and fairly.

scenes.animation: Three stacked layers appear like floors of a building: 'Lok Sabha: national level', 'State Legislative Assembly: state level', 'Local bodies: city and village level'. A map of India splits into 543 small constituency pieces.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Citizens vote at many levels: the Lok Sabha at the national level, legislative assemblies at the state level, and local bodies in cities and villages.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: For the Lok Sabha, India is divided into 543 constituencies.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Those elected to the Lok Sabha are Members of Parliament, or MPs. Those elected to state assemblies are Members of Legislative Assembly, or MLAs.

scenes.animation: Two cartoon representatives stand side by side: an MP in front of the Parliament building labelled 'National issues', and an MLA in front of a state assembly labelled 'Regional issues'. A signboard lists names 'Vidhan Sabha' and 'Niyama Sabha'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So what's the difference between an MP and an MLA?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: MPs represent us in the national Parliament and focus on issues of the whole country. MLAs represent us in the state assembly and focus mainly on regional issues.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The state assembly has many regional names, like Vidhan Sabha or Niyama Sabha.

scenes.animation: A finish-line race: three candidates run, a flag reads 'First-Past-the-Post'. The one crossing first wins, even though a pie chart above him shows only 36% of votes. A flashback bubble shows Gurmat's '12 out of 33'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: India uses the First-Past-the-Post system. The candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So a candidate can win without getting even 50 per cent of the votes, just like Gurmat won with 12 out of 33.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: 'most votes' is not the same as 'majority of votes'. Examiners love this difference.

scenes.animation: A seat chart of the Lok Sabha fills in: 84 seats coloured 'SC', 47 'ST' and 412 'General'. Then a flowchart: 'Party or coalition wins majority of seats' leads to 'Forms government' leads to 'Leader becomes Prime Minister'; a parallel state track ends in 'Chief Minister'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In the Lok Sabha, 84 constituencies are reserved for scheduled castes and 47 for scheduled tribes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: After voting, the party or coalition that wins a majority of seats forms the national government. Its leader typically becomes the Prime Minister.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A coalition is two or more parties working together. In a state, the leader of the majority becomes the Chief Minister.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a Parliament icon and a state assembly icon. Points appear: '1. 543 Lok Sabha constituencies elect MPs; states elect MLAs', '2. First-Past-the-Post: most votes wins', '3. Majority of seats forms the government; leader becomes PM or CM'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: 543 Lok Sabha constituencies elect MPs, while state assembly constituencies elect MLAs.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: in First-Past-the-Post, the candidate with the most votes wins.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the party or coalition with a majority of seats forms the government, and its leader becomes Prime Minister or Chief Minister.

chapter: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
name: Indirect Elections and the Road Ahead

scenes.animation: At Suryodaya School, class representatives from every class walk into a room labelled 'School Council' and cast votes, while ordinary students watch through the window. Zippy presses his face to the glass.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Hey, why can't the rest of us vote for the school council?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Because the class reps vote on your behalf. That's an indirect election, and India uses it too.

scenes.animation: A flowchart builds: 'MLAs' arrow to 'Elect 233 Rajya Sabha members', and 'President of India' arrow to 'Nominates 12'. The total '245' glows. A map shows Uttar Pradesh with many seat icons and Arunachal Pradesh with few.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Members of the Rajya Sabha are also MPs, but they are chosen through indirect elections.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Of its 245 members, 233 are elected by MLAs, and the President nominates 12.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Seats depend on population, so Uttar Pradesh has more seats than Arunachal Pradesh.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: MLAs vote using a single transferable vote system, ranking candidates by preference.

scenes.animation: A clock ticks; every two years, one-third of the Rajya Sabha seats light up and are refilled, while the house itself never goes dark. Labels: 'Permanent House', 'Term: 6 years', '1/3 retire every 2 years'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Rajya Sabha is called the Permanent House. It is never dissolved.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Each member has a six-year term, and one-third of the members retire every two years.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: the Lok Sabha is directly elected, while the Rajya Sabha is indirectly elected. This comparison is frequently asked.

scenes.animation: An 'Electoral College' box fills with MPs from both Houses and elected MLAs of states, Delhi and Puducherry, who drop ballots in. Nominated members and legislative council members stand outside with a 'Not included' sign. A second box for the Vice President fills with all MPs, elected and nominated.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The President is elected by an electoral college of elected MPs of both Houses and elected MLAs of the states, Delhi and Puducherry.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Nominated members do not vote. This way, only directly elected representatives choose the President.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Vice President is elected by all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated. The Vice President chairs the Rajya Sabha.

scenes.animation: Three storm clouds float over a ballot box: 'Money power', 'Candidates with criminal records', 'Voter apathy in cities'. A young voter with a lantern marked 'Awareness' pushes the clouds away.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Our system faces challenges: the influence of money, candidates with criminal records, and voter apathy, especially in cities.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The answer is informed voters. An aware and vigilant voter is the strongest safeguard of democracy.

scenes.animation: Recap board with icons for the Rajya Sabha, the President's residence and a lantern. Points appear: '1. Rajya Sabha: 233 elected by MLAs + 12 nominated', '2. President and VP chosen by electoral colleges', '3. Aware voters meet democracy's challenges'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: the Rajya Sabha has 233 members elected by MLAs and 12 nominated by the President.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: the President and Vice President are chosen by electoral colleges, not directly by the people.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: aware, vigilant voters are the answer to democracy's challenges.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Vigilant voter reporting for duty!
